text:
maria: Hey team, kickoff for FalconX migration POC tomorrow. Main asks from their SRE: ensure fallback routing parity and confirm token billing deltas. short window.
jon: quick Q — what do they call a fallback in their API? header-based region fallback or model family fallback?
maria: they do region-first, then model-family. header is `X-Fallback-Policy: region,model`. they expect 503->auto-retry to a warm standby.
elaine: ok — runtime supports model-family fallback already, region routing is policy layer. we can mirror behaviour but need to confirm cooldowns and backoff.
jon: also note their client retries on 429 with exponential backoff up to 3 tries. we should match so token billing for retries is comparable.
amy: pricing question from buyer: will retries be charged as normal tokens? they want committed forecast parity.
saleh: security check — we need to answer the questionnaire bit about logs on fallback. they require that request/response bodies are not logged on fallback attempts unless debug mode and sampled. is that acceptable?
jon: yes — our default is no payload logs for retries; we only log headers + decision reason. we can provide an opt-in debug mode in the POC staging with sampling.
elaine: small implementation note: tokenizer differences mean responses can be 2-7% token-different vs their vendor. that shows up in billing deltas. recommend showing them a side-by-side token-count report during the POC.
maria: can we generate that automatically in the POC harness? buyer wants weekly delta report.
jon: yes — we can dump per-request token counts and group by prompt template. sample snippet in the harness:
```
# pseudocode
resp = client.generate(prompt)
metrics.log({"request_id": id, "tokens": resp.token_count, "model": resp.model})
```
elaine: and we can add a normalization layer to trim trailing whitespace/stop tokens before counting to reduce noise.
amy: on pricing, propose: hosted parity for first 3 months with capped retry billing (cap 3 retries per request), after that revert to normal usage. gives them runway.
maria: they asked about canaries/rollbacks for the adapter. can we do a staged traffic split by user token?
jon: yes — console supports per-token routing rules. can do 10/30/60 splits and automatic rollback on error-rate spikes. infra-bot: deploy pipeline for canary created: pipeline/poC-falconx-canary #1423 :rocket:
saleh: send me the security questionnaire items about fallback, logs, encryption at rest, KMS. I'll answer and ping legal if needed.
maria: assigned: @saleh for security, @jon for routing behaviour doc, @elaine for token-reporting harness, @amy for pricing proposal. I'll own buyer comms.
amy: I'll put together the commercial note and draft the 3-month capped-retry appendix.
jon: one last thing — rate-limit headers differ. their API uses `X-RateLimit-Remaining` while ours uses `X-RW-Quota-Left`. propose mapping those in the adapter layer to avoid client changes.
elaine: yep, mapping sounds good. also add a small feature flag to echo their header names during the POC.
maria: perfect. we'll demo fallback + token delta report in the Wednesday call. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
saleh: noted, sending questionnaire answers by EOD tomorrow.
amy: commercial note ready by tomorrow noon.
jon: routing doc PR will be up in a few hours.
elaine: harness repo link (internal): <https://git.redwood.ai/poC/falconx-token-harness> — will add instructions.
maria: awesome. closing loop. anyone else see blockers?
jon: none from infra side. will surface if latency/kv-cache affects retries.
saleh: none. I'll double-check retention settings.
infra-bot: reminder: staging infra scheduled maintenance at 1845555000 UTC — might affect canary window.
maria: noted, we'll avoid that maintenance window. thanks everyone.
